fields.hint: Ask which of these two tools a project with exactly one source file and no imports would still need.
fields.explanation: A compiler translates source from one form into another — TypeScript to JavaScript, modern syntax to older syntax, C to machine code — largely file by file. A bundler resolves the import graph and combines modules into the artifacts you ship. Minification is an optional step either can perform, neither runs in the browser during a normal build, and type checking is tsc's own job: SWC works file by file and never consults the type system.

problems: explanation claimed 'it is the compiler, not the bundler, that type-checks' while the stem names SWC, which does not type-check at all
hint states both halves of the distinction the item asks for, so the key can be matched without knowing either tool
evidence: fetched: https://swc.rs/docs/migrating-from-tsc - 'SWC works on file-by-file, so any code transforms that depend on understanding the full type system will not work'
knowledge: bundlers (Vite/Rollup, webpack, esbuild in bundle mode) resolve the import graph into output chunks, which no per-file compiler does
notes: The key itself is sound; the type-checking sentence was the one claim the stem's own example contradicts.

evidence: fetched: https://v8.dev/docs/ignition - 'V8 features an interpreter called Ignition. Ignition is a fast low-level register-based interpreter', so the explanation's 'source, or bytecode derived from it' is accurate and the old 'statement by statement' gloss is correctly gone
knowledge: a .js file executes under Node or a browser with no compiled artifact on disk, while an ahead-of-time compiler emits one
notes: The hint names the artifact axis but both artifact-shaped options sit on it, so the discrimination still requires knowing which way round they go; American 'artifact' now used throughout.
